tools.name: list_metrics
tools.description: Every metric there is a figure for, with its unit and the first and last day. Use the exact metric names from here in query_metrics.

tools.name: query_metrics
tools.description: Each day's figures as the Metrics Nest app shows them, or weekly or monthly buckets. One row per metric and day (one per reading for metrics read reading by reading), already combined: food and water include what was logged in the app and what other apps wrote to Health, so never add rows together.

tools.name: query_intraday
tools.description: Hour-by-hour readings such as heart rate, kept 90 days. One row per metric, hour and device. Needs the intraday category.

tools.name: list_nights
tools.description: One row per night, keyed by the morning it ended on: bed and wake times, and seconds asleep and in each stage. With several devices, the longest sleep is the night. get_night has the stages.

tools.name: get_night
tools.description: One night in full, including the stage-by-stage hypnogram.

tools.name: list_workouts
tools.description: Workouts with activity, start and end, duration, distance, energy, the heart rate summary and the note. Sets and the route are on get_workout.

tools.name: get_workout
tools.description: One workout in full: the heart rate trace (average bpm and how many readings, minute by minute from the start) and zones, and the exercises and sets and the route when they were shared.

tools.name: query_logs
tools.description: What the person logged in the app: food with calories, macros and fruit and veg portions, drinks by kind (coffee, water, alcohol...), and typed weight. Each entry carries its time and part of day: morning, midday, evening or late. For a day's totals, use query_metrics.

tools.name: list_exercises
tools.description: Every exercise logged in a workout (bench press, squat...), most recently done first, with how many workouts it was in, the first and last day, the heaviest weight lifted in kg (best_weight_kg), and the muscles it trains (null where the person never said, for an exercise of their own). tools.name: muscle_sets

tools.name: list_clients
tools.description: For a coach: the people who approved you as their coach, with what each lets you read and from when. Pass a client id as `client` to any other tool to read that person. A client who stopped sharing shows as ended.

tools.name: list_goals
tools.description: The goals set in the app: daily or weekly targets on a metric (a calorie ceiling, a water or step target) and journeys toward a value (a weight to reach), each with its progress as the phone last computed it. Needs the goals category.

tools.name: goal_history
tools.description: One goal's progress day by day, newest first: the figure, the fraction of the way there and whether it was met, as the phone computed it on each sync. Use it for how a goal has gone, not only where it stands. The id is from list_goals.

tools.name: list_badges
tools.description: The badges earned in the app, with tier and the time each was earned. Needs the goals category.

tools.name: propose_workout
tools.description: Suggest a workout for the person to approve in the Metrics Nest app. This only leaves a suggestion: nothing is planned until they approve it on their phone, where they can also edit or reject it, and no workout is ever created, changed or deleted here. tools.name: list_exercise_catalog
tools.description: Every exercise the Metrics Nest app offers, with the exercise_id propose_workout takes for it, its name and other names, its group, and the muscles it trains. The same for everybody; list_exercises is what this person has actually done.

tools.name: list_saved_workouts
tools.description: The workouts the person saved in the Metrics Nest app to start whenever they like ("Leg day", "Push A"), each with its id, exercises, sets and reps. propose_removing_saved_workout takes the id; propose_saved_workout adds a new one.

tools.name: propose_saved_workout
tools.description: Suggest a named workout for the person to keep and start whenever they like ("Leg day"), rather than a session on one day (that is propose_workout). tools.description: Suggest taking one of the person's saved workouts away. Nothing is removed until they approve it in the Metrics Nest app; the workouts already done from it stay. The id is from list_saved_workouts.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: exercise_history · Public sink: get_profile, query_metrics, propose_workout, propose_meal · Destructive: list_proposals.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: exercise_history · Public sink: get_profile, query_metrics, propose_workout, propose_meal · Destructive: list_proposals

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
